Strait of Hormuz Status: October 16, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  229 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
16 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.17 + 0.86 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 BBC and CNBC report ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz have hit a record high, with Singapore-flagged vessels among those struck.

02 Iran's army chief says the strait will remain closed until the Iranian people's rights are respected, per IRNA and WANA News Agency.

03 Brent stood at $105.17, up 0.86% over 24 hours, as of 09:17 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to normal commercial traffic, with BBC News reporting that ship attacks near the waterway have now reached a record high. Singapore-registered vessels are among those struck, per CNBC. Separately, euronews.com reports another tanker caught fire near the eastern strait after two cargo ships sank in attacks; that report originates with Iranian state media. IRNA, citing Iran's army chief, states the strait will not reopen until the Iranian people's rights are respected, a position that WANA News Agency also carries; this is an Iranian state media claim and has not been independently verified in this feed. On the throughput picture, IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; that multi-day lag is expected given PortWatch's weekly publication schedule. Our feed indexed 77 headlines in the last 24 hours, though several rows typically track the same underlying story. Brent crude stood at $105.17, up 0.86% over 24 hours, as of 09:17 UTC; WTI stood at $97.05. A BBC fact-check found no evidence that a viral video purporting to show ships stuck in the strait in 2026 is genuine. The policy deadlock persists: Iranian officials have reiterated conditions for reopening, and no published US response has resolved the gap. As of 09:22 UTC, 118 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
